subject: Risk & Compliance
title: Supply Chain Attacks
description: A quick, practical guide to Supply Chain Attacks.

hook.text: You secure your own network perfectly. But your software vendor gets hacked, and the malware flows to you.

buildup.text: Supply chain attacks target the weakest link — vendors, contractors, and third-party software providers.

discovery.text: The SolarWinds and Kaseya attacks showed how one compromised vendor can infect thousands of customers.

twist.text: Companies often have hundreds of vendors with access to their systems. Monitoring them all is nearly impossible.

climax.text: Your security is only as strong as your weakest vendor. Third-party risk is now a top board concern.

punchline.text: You're secure. Your vendor isn't. Now you're not.

quiz.question: What makes supply chain attacks so dangerous?
options: One compromised vendor can infect thousands of customers
They are easy to detect in advance
